thread.title: South Dakota Girl Scout CEO helps develop new cookie flavor
thread.title_full: South Dakota Girl Scout CEO helps develop new cookie flavor

author: Tanya Manus Journal staff
title: South Dakota Girl Scout CEO helps develop new cookie flavor
text:
A Girl Scout Cookie inspired by Rocky Road ice cream is coming in 2026, and South Dakota’s Marla Meyer is one of the tastemakers behind the new sweet treat.
The Exploremores Girl Scout Cookie blends the flavors of chocolate, marshmallow and toasted almond-flavored creme into a sandwich cookie. The announcement in early September about the new Exploremores notes the cookie’s name captures the limitless spirit of exploration that drives Girl Scouts, and that “life’s more fun when you explore more!”
Meyer has been part of the start-to-finish cookie development process for two Girl Scout Cookie flavors – Exploremores and the chocolate-caramel Adventurefuls introduced in 2022.
She is the CEO of Girl Scouts Dakota Horizons, a nonprofit organization that serves more than 10,000 members in South Dakota, North Dakota, Minnesota and Iowa. She’ll celebrate her 10th anniversary as CEO in October.
As a Girl Scout executive, troop helper and the mother of a Girl Scout who sells the cookies, developing a new cookie is a project near to Meyer’s heart.
“It’s a tough job, but somebody has to do it,” Meyer chuckled.
Meyer happily taste-tested dozens of cookies to help choose the flavor profile for Exploremores, but she said creating a new cookie is a process that takes years as the cookie flavor is developed, tested, named and its packaging is designed.
While consumers always want iconic Girl Scout Cookies such as Thin Mints and Samoas, Meyer said Girl Scouts often get questions during cookie season about what’s new.
“We take a look at current consumer trends, future consumer trends, what we have in our (cookie flavor) portfolio,” Meyer said. “People are buying Girl Scout Cookies for a treat, so what’s happening in the world of treats? … If we’re bringing a new one in, it’s got to be solid. We spend a lot of time on what the concept is going to be.”
“You’re determining things like the flavor profile but also what kind of cookie is it (such as a sandwich cookie). You work with wonderful bakers and they have incredible food scientists that bring the flavors together, and then we do consumer testing,” Meyer said.
“We really work to streamline it so whatever cookie we come out with, every girl across the country can sell the same cookie,” she said.
Meyer’s previous career was in consumer package goods, a skillset that seamlessly fits the task of cookie development. When she went to work for Girl Scouts – Dakota Horizons, she applied to be on the Girl Scouts’ National Product Program Committee, and she’s now the committee co-chair.
The committee is a small group that’s very hands-on with the national strategy of the Girl Scout Cookie Program. Meyer also is a member of a subcommittee that focuses on innovation of new cookie flavors.
“It’s interesting to work with the science behind this,” Meyer said. “Nailing that chocolate flavor, that taste of marshmallow and this little bit of toasted almond is a really interesting combination, and then you’re talking about what’s in the cream and what’s in the cookie and what color is it? It’s a really cool cookie.”
Girl Scouts USA works with two bakers, ABC Bakers and Little Brownie Bakers, to produce all the Girl Scout Cookies sold nationwide.
“They’re incredible partners. … They are for sure the experts and they are involved, whether it’s influencing a flavor or making a suggestion on a concept, we’re doing that together. They work with the subcommittee,” Meyer said. “They are a huge part. They take the concept and do a tremendous amount of the development. … They help us get to where we have an amazing cookie.”
Girl Scouts USA works with the cookie development team to implement consumer testing before any new cookie flavor is launched.
“It’s pretty in-depth to make sure that (a new flavor) is not just a hunch, that this will be a winner,” she said. “There’s enough data and research along the way that we have a good idea on how it’s going to perform.”
“We’re trying to make sure we nail it for the girls to be able to have this incredible item in their cookie lineup,” Meyer said.
The Girl Scout Cookie Program has existed for more than 100 years and is perpetually innovating. Meyer said new cookie flavor ideas are in the works for 2028 and 2030.
Building confidence, business skills, adventures
The Exploremores cookies will be sold during the 2026 Girl Scout Cookie season, which runs locally from mid-February to mid- March. To be notified when cookie sales start, text “Cookies” to 59618.
All proceeds from cookie sales stay local with Girl Scout councils and troops to help fund life-changing programs and experiences all year long.
“We want folks to remember the girls are running businesses, they’re learning skills,” Meyer said. “When you’re purchasing cookies, it’s a great treat for you, and it’s coming back to your community through much of the community service Girl Scouts do as well as leadership they are providing today and in the future for their communities.”
Ultimately, the scouts who sell the cookies and their success are at the heart of developing new cookies, Meyer said. Scouts who attend Cookie University to prepare for the annual cookie sales will be to sample the new Exploremores. Cookie University gives scouts the skills to become successful cookie entrepreneurs.
Using age-appropriate lessons, Cookie University introduces girls to money management, decision making, goal setting, people skills and business ethics. Scouts also build their own digital storefronts, have QR codes and make pitch videos as part of their cookie-selling tools.
Girl Scouts – Dakota Horizons will host Cookie University in Rapid City on Jan. 31, 2026. Go to gsdakotahorizons.org to register and for more information. Cookie University is for Scouts in kindergarten through 12th grade, with advanced Beyond Cookie University curriculum for middle school and high school Scouts.
“I’m proud every day, and the outcomes are so real. You see it in the girls and the things they’re accomplishing themselves or doing for their community. There’s hundreds and hundreds of projects across our council every year that are directly girls doing things and bringing it back to their community. They’re also their communities’ future leaders,” Meyer said.
